# MemoX v3 — Foundations (run ONCE, before any component spec)

HANDOFF MODE: FOUNDATIONS

This run owns the GLOBAL visual system only — palette, type, spacing, radius,
icon and elevation scales, composition fundamentals, responsive and
system-owned rules. It does not own screen layout, component variants,
feature states or business flow.

Source: MemoX v3 HTML design kit (ui_kits/mobile/v3). Every value below is read live from
colors_and_type.css at page load, for both themes, so it cannot drift from the
design. Load this once as shared context; each component spec that follows is
written against it and will not repeat these values.

## Visual direction

MemoX runs two themes from one structure: Tokyo Pure Light, a cool blue-tinted
white where every neutral carries a trace of indigo and nothing is warm; and
Tokyo Nebula, a deep navy dark theme where the brand indigo lifts for contrast
rather than the surfaces inverting. The language is flat and quiet — surfaces
separate by a one-pixel hairline and a very soft shadow, not by heavy elevation.
Indigo carries every primary action, violet is the signature accent, and green
is reserved for mastery and success so it always reads as progress. Type is set
in a single sans with a tight-tracked display face for figures, and the layout
keeps a steady 16px gutter with generous card interiors.

## Colors

the same — it is NOT a claim of invariance. Only inverseSurface and
onInverseSurface are intentionally invariant among these standard roles;
elsewhere an equal pair is a coincidence, and a token whose name says fixed may
still flip (mastery-fixed).

## Elevation / border / shadow

Surfaces separate by a hairline plus a very soft shadow — there is no heavy
elevation anywhere in this design.

  border         1px solid outlineVariant on cards, inputs and dividers
  card           0 12px 32px rgba(15,22,56,0.10)
  chrome         0 -2px 12px rgba(15,22,56,0.05)
  floating       0 8px 24px rgba(15,22,56,0.12)
  scrim          scrim at 45% alpha behind dialogs and sheets
  glass chrome   translucent surface + backdrop blur on the bottom nav

Hierarchy: page ground → card (hairline + card shadow) → sheet/dialog
(container surface + scrim) → floating action (fab shadow). Shadows are neutral,
never tinted with the brand color.

## Screen composition

The component sits on the 16px screen gutter, in a single content column.
Vertical rhythm around it: 12 between related rows, 16 between list items,
24 between sections, 32 between major groups. Card interiors are 20.
Scrollable content clears pinned chrome by 48 at the tail so the last item is
never trapped under the bottom nav or the floating action.
Hierarchy on any screen using it: primary focal surface → supporting metadata →
primary action (anchored) → secondary action (inline, lower contrast).

## Responsive / Android notes

  compact phone   the content column narrows; the gutter stays 16. Nothing
                  in this design depends on a fixed viewport width.
  large text      every text container must grow. Do not clamp text scale and
                  do not put a fixed height around text.
  landscape       the column stays single; pinned chrome remains reachable.
  keyboard open   the focused field and the primary action stay reachable; the
                  IME inset is supplied at runtime, never hardcoded.

SYSTEM-OWNED geometry — Android supplies all of it:
  status bar · display cutout · gesture/navigation inset · keyboard inset ·
  system Back. The kit's 44px status bar and its phone bezel are preview
  chrome. Never convert them into application dimensions.

## HTML/JSX translation notes

  WEB TECHNIQUE   the FAB is absolutely positioned inside the frame. The bottom
                  nav and every commit footer are NOT — they are in-flow
                  siblings of the scroll and never overlap it
  VISUAL INTENT   the floating action stays anchored above the content and clear
                  of the system inset; bottom chrome occupies its own space
  HANDOFF         preserve the anchored relationship for the FAB and the
                  in-flow relationship for the bars; absolute positioning is
                  not part of the design

  WEB TECHNIQUE   a ::after box widening a small control's tap area
  VISUAL INTENT   the painted control stays compact while the tap area meets
                  48px
  HANDOFF         keep visual size and hit area separate; the technique is
                  irrelevant

  WEB TECHNIQUE   backdrop-filter blur on the bottom nav
  VISUAL INTENT   chrome reads as translucent glass over scrolling content
  HANDOFF         reproduce the visual result; a solid surface at the same
                  value is acceptable if blur is costly

  WEB TECHNIQUE   color-mix() overlays for hover and pressed tints
  VISUAL INTENT   a percentage tint of the role color over the surface
  HANDOFF         use the platform's own overlay mechanism at the same
                  percentage

  WEB TECHNIQUE   Scrim / Dialog / BottomSheet are absolutely positioned with
                  inset:0 INSIDE the phone div, and Dialog and BottomSheet each
                  draw their own Scrim unless passed scrim={false}
  VISUAL INTENT   a modal layer covering the app surface, dimmed to 45% of the
                  scrim role color, with the panel centred (dialog) or
                  bottom-anchored (sheet)
  HANDOFF         the platform's own modal route owns the barrier and the full
                  window — the scrim={false} flag exists only because this mock
                  nests overlays inside a preview frame. Do NOT carry it across
                  as a widget parameter; take the dim percentage, the panel
                  geometry and the motion, nothing else.

  WEB TECHNIQUE   TextField and SearchField are static mocks — a <span> holding
                  placeholder text plus a CSS-animated caret, not a real input
  VISUAL INTENT   the rest / focus / error appearance of a filled field
  HANDOFF         "focused" and "error" here are VISUAL STATES, not behaviour.
                  Real focus, caret, selection, IME and validation are the
                  platform's; only the borders, fill and message styling transfer.

  Also do not copy: hover-only affordances (there is no hover on Android), the
  fake status bar, the device bezel, or any fixed pixel box drawn around text.

## Priorities

  P0  palette and both themes; type scale; 16 gutter and the spacing rhythm
  P1  this component's surface treatment, radius, geometry class and states
  P2  icon sizing per role, hairline and shadow treatment
  P3  decorative polish — flip timing, glass blur, the skeleton's opacity
      pulse (0.45 ↔ 0.75 over 1.4s — a pulse, not a shimmer sweep)


## Implementation handoff — foundations

GLOBAL VISUAL TOKENS:
  spacing 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/48 · radius 4/8/12/16/20/24/999
  icons 16/20/24/32/40 · touch target 48 minimum

COLOR / THEME SPEC:
  two themes, light / dark, in the Colors section above. inverseSurface and
  onInverseSurface are the intentionally invariant pair. tertiary is the violet
  accent; green is reserved for mastery.

TYPOGRAPHY:
  12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 40, 12 is a hard floor, not on the 4dp grid

COMPONENT CONTRACTS:
  supplied per component, in the specs that follow this one — each carries its
  own dimension table, icon list and state matrix

SCREEN COMPOSITION:
  16 gutter · 16 list gap · 24 section gap · 32 major separation · 48 scroll tail

RESPONSIVE RULES:
  single column, no fixed widths, no fixed heights around text, no text-scale
  clamping, pinned chrome always reachable

# MemoX v3 — Flutter theme implementation prerequisite

RUN ORDER: FOUNDATIONS → **THIS** → shared components → screens.
This is NOT a fourth handoff mode and NOT a design layer: it is the binding
step between the design Foundations and ONE common Flutter theme. No shared
component task is runnable until it is done.

## How to read this document

This step has two structured sources, each authoritative for ONE thing:

  themeRegistry              source of truth for THEME SEMANTIC BINDING: kind,
                             value, destination, alias evidence, derivation,
                             usage status, runtime disposition
  widgets[*].themeRoleUsage  source of truth for COMPONENT THEME CONSUMPTION:
                             slot, state, access, role / child configuration /
                             instance input, treatment

FOUNDATIONS stays authoritative for the rest of the design truth — typography,
spacing, geometry, sizing, motion. This step BINDS those values to the
repository's theme; it does not author them, and where a number here comes from
Foundations it is rendered from the same source the Foundations spec renders.

Every theme table, consumer list and index in this document is a GENERATED VIEW
over the two sources above. Editing the prose changes nothing. If a value here
is wrong, the registry or the component's usage record is wrong — fix it there
and regenerate.

## Repository inspection — do this first

Inspect the existing Flutter repository before changing anything. Identify:

  current ThemeData construction · light and dark ColorScheme definitions ·
  the current TextTheme · existing theme extensions / semantic-colour layers ·
  existing spacing / radius / sizing token classes · existing Material
  component-theme configuration · existing shared-widget theming conventions

Reuse and extend the canonical implementation. Do not create a parallel theme
system, and do not replace a larger canonical role set with this smaller
V3-specific palette.

## Theme architecture rules

  1. Standard Material colour semantics resolve through the ColorScheme.
  2. MemoX product SEMANTIC COLOURS that Material has no honest role for
     resolve through ONE semantic-colour mechanism the repository already has;
     introduce the smallest compatible extension only if none exists. This
     rule covers MEMOX_SEMANTIC_COLOR only — every other kind routes to its own
     destination (DERIVED_COLOR to central derivation, DECORATION to the
     decoration/token mechanism, STATE_TOKEN to the global state policy,
     EFFECT_TOKEN to the effect mechanism, M3_ALIAS to its ColorScheme role).
  3. Typography resolves through the shared TextTheme / canonical typography.
  4. Spacing, radius, control dimensions, icon sizes and the touch minimum
     belong to the repository's design-token system — never to ColorScheme.
  5. Component-specific geometry stays in the component contract; screen
     arrangement stays in the screen composition.
  6. If V3 does not determine a role the repository already defines (the
     Fixed family, container roles V3 never paints), PRESERVE the existing
     canonical definition. Do not invent a V3 colour to fill it, and do not
     delete the role. Report what you preserved.

## Runtime theme size control — read before you add a field

GENERATED VIEW from themeRegistry.implementationDisposition.

DO NOT create a theme field for every Foundation semantic just because it
appears in this registry. The design registry is deliberately LARGER than the
runtime semantic extension, and that is allowed.

  BIND_NOW       28 semantics — the current V3 implementation needs them;
                 make sure the common theme can provide them
  PRESERVE_ONLY  15 semantics — Foundation/design truth with no active V3
                 consumer path. Keep them documented, keep an existing repo
                 definition if one is already there, and do NOT add a new
                 unused field for them.

BIND_NOW does NOT mean "put it in the MemoX semantic extension". Each semantic
is routed by its KIND, and only some kinds store a value of their own:

  the existing MemoX semantic-colour mechanism
    mastery · warning · on-warning · status-new · status-learning · status-reviewing · status-mastered · error-fill · on-error-fill
  ColorScheme — resolve to the target role, no new field [stores nothing]
    bg · surface-muted · surface-raised · progress-track · text-secondary
  central colour derivation
    danger-soft · danger-border · warning-soft · surface-hero · chrome-glass
  the decoration / token mechanism
    shadow-soft · shadow-card · shadow-chrome · shadow-fab · border-ghost
  the global state-token / policy mechanism
    op-disabled · op-press
  the effect / token mechanism
    op-glass · glass-blur

  PRESERVE_ONLY (same routing when a definition already exists; add nothing new)
    success · streak · on-streak · mastery-fixed · on-danger · text-muted · badge-bg · danger · text-primary · primary-soft · primary-border · success-soft · shadow-none · border-strong · op-hover

This rule governs MemoX-specific semantics only; it never shrinks the canonical
M3 ColorScheme role set below.

## Light / dark theme requirements

Both themes are complete and first-class: Tokyo Pure Light and Tokyo Nebula.
Dark is not a filter over light — the values are authored.

Among V3-authored standard M3 colour roles, inverseSurface and onInverseSurface
are intentionally invariant:

  inverse-surface       #34395D
  on-inverse-surface    #E8EAFC

That claim is scoped and asserted, not inferred: the registry stamps
invariant:true on exactly these roles and the validator fails if either value
differs between themes. It says nothing about the rest of the registry. Other
tokens may happen to carry the same value in both themes without being
invariant, and a token whose NAME says fixed may still flip — mastery-fixed is
#C7F2D8 light / #1F4A37 dark. Never read invariance off equal values or off a
token name; read it off the invariant flag.

## Typography / TextTheme binding

The SAME seven roles the Foundations spec states — one scale, rendered from one
source, so the two steps cannot disagree:

  role            size  weight  line-height  tracking   usage
  caption         12    600     1.4          1.2px      overlines, metadata, chips, counts — hard 12px floor
  body            14    400     1.5          0          default running text
  body large      16    500     1.5          0          list titles, emphasised body
  title           20    700     1.2          -0.64px    section and screen titles
  headline        24    700     1.2          -0.64px    screen headline
  display         32    800     1.1          -0.64px    hero figure
  stat            40    600     1.0          -0.64px    large metric, tabular numerals

Establish this once as the shared typography source. Button, Card, ListRow,
SettingsRow and every other shared widget consume it; none of them creates its
own text styles.

A component contract may state a type treatment of its own (the app-bar content
title at 20/700/-0.3px, the button label at 14/600/0.1px). Those are COMPONENT
rows, not additions to this scale: implement them as a component-level override
of the nearest role above, never as a new global text style.

## Global state semantics

The GLOBAL layer owns exactly three things:

  disabled          opacity 0.38 over the whole control — ONE value everywhere
  pressed           platform state overlay at op-press (0.12)
  focused           2px primary ring, offset 2 — one treatment for every control

  hover             web only; Android has no hover state — do not implement

Everything else is COMPONENT-owned, because it is not uniform across the kit:

  selected / checked / active    each component states its own role mapping
                                 (FilterChip swaps fill → primary and label →
                                 onPrimary; OptionRow thickens a ring; BottomNav
                                 tints a pill). Do not generalise one of them
                                 into a global rule.
  error presentation             the theme owns the error COLOUR semantics; the
                                 component owns whether there is a border, a
                                 message, where it sits and which slots change.
                                 The border-plus-message-line treatment belongs
                                 to TextField / SearchField, not to every control.

A component spec REFERENCES the three global rules; it never redefines them.

## Theme implementation sequence

   1. Inspect the repository's existing theme architecture.
   2. Enumerate the complete canonical M3 ColorScheme role set.
   3. Reconcile dispositions: V3_DEFINED vs REPO_PRESERVED (table above).
   4. Build / reconcile the Light ColorScheme.
   5. Build / reconcile the Dark ColorScheme.
   6. Verify the full canonical role set is still present.
   7. Bind the EXACT Foundations typography to the repository's TextTheme.
   8. Route each BIND_NOW entry BY KIND — only BIND_NOW MEMOX_SEMANTIC_COLOR
      entries use the MemoX semantic-colour mechanism; an alias resolves to its
      ColorScheme target, and no field is added for a PRESERVE_ONLY entry.
   9. Bind DERIVED_COLOR values centrally, each derivation exactly once.
  10. Bind DECORATION treatments centrally where the token architecture allows.
  11. Establish the global STATE_TOKEN policies: disabled, pressed, focus — and
      keep EFFECT_TOKEN values out of them.
  12. Configure Material component-theme defaults only where they represent
      the V3 baseline accurately.
  13. Validate the common theme on its own — including Foundation semantic-role
      coverage, every IMPLEMENT_COMPONENT theme usage, and aggregate
      role-consumer consistency.
  14. Freeze this prerequisite.
  15. Only then start the IMPLEMENT_COMPONENT tasks.

## Ownership matrix

  AREA                          OWNER
  standard Material colours     ColorScheme
  MemoX semantic colours        one semantic theme mechanism
  derived colours               central derivation in the theme layer
  typography                    TextTheme / canonical typography
  global interaction states     common state-token policy
  visual effect configuration   the effect/decoration token layer
  spacing / radius / sizing     the design-token system
  decoration, shadow, borders   the canonical decoration/token mechanism
  Material global defaults      ThemeData component themes, where appropriate
  shared-widget variants        the shared component
  screen composition            the screen

Which repository classes carry each row is Claude Code's decision after
inspection.

## Material component-theme policy

Inspect these categories and decide, per category, whether a central Material
component theme represents the V3 default honestly: buttons · text/input
fields · dialogs · navigation · chips · switch/toggle · snackbar · bottom sheet
· progress indicators.

  If a Material component theme can carry the V3 global default without
  fighting the MemoX variants → configure it centrally.
  If the MemoX contract is richer than the Material theme can express cleanly
  → keep the variation in the shared component, which still consumes
  ColorScheme, TextTheme and the global tokens.

Do not force everything into ThemeData; do not leave everything local.

## Shared-component consumption rules

Shared components declare slot/state → role usage and consume the theme. They
must not: hard-code a V3 hex; copy a standard role into a custom layer;
redefine a MemoX semantic role locally; re-resolve a role this step already
resolved; or reach into another shared component's theme roles.

## Theme gaps and UNSPECIFIED handling

A role a component needs that this step did not establish is a DEPENDENCY GAP:
report it upstream. It is not UNSPECIFIED, and it is never a licence for a
widget to patch in a colour. UNSPECIFIED stays what the frozen template says:
the design does not determine the value — keep the repository convention where
that is safe, ask where geometry, state, interaction, content loss or
accessibility depends on it.

## Validation — verify after implementing

  light ColorScheme complete · dark ColorScheme complete · the repository's
  existing canonical M3 role set still intact · every V3-defined standard role
  resolving through ColorScheme · every BIND_NOW entry routed by its KIND, with
  only MEMOX_SEMANTIC_COLOR entries in the MemoX semantic mechanism · no new
  field for a PRESERVE_ONLY semantic · TextTheme shared ·
  disabled/pressed/focus shared · glass opacity and blur outside the state
  layer · no raw colour duplicated in a shared widget · no widget running a
  private theme system · Material defaults centralized where appropriate ·
  custom variants still reading the common theme

Report every mismatch instead of inventing a value.

GENERATED VIEW from widgets[*].themeRoleUsage where access == VIA_COMPONENT.

These parents paint nothing. They ask another shared component for a semantic

derivedColorConsistency.note: §21: the derivation is owned by Theme Binding, so a component consuming a DERIVED_COLOR carries treatment FULL_STRENGTH. A component that tints a BASE role itself binds that base role with an explicit treatment instead. Declared mix percentages are checked against the authored color-mix() expressions, and a derivation that names an opacity token must carry exactly that value.

# StatusBar — design specification for Flutter handoff

HANDOFF MODE: COMPONENT
IMPLEMENTATION ACTION: USE_PLATFORM
  Do NOT build a widget. The platform supplies this; configure it.

Source: MemoX v3 HTML design kit · A · Chrome & navigation
NON-BINDING MATERIAL ANALOGY: the platform status bar — no app widget exists for it
  Orientation only. Inspect the repository and map this contract onto what is
  already there — do not read the analogy as a widget tree to reproduce.

> Run the MemoX Foundations spec ONCE before this prompt. It carries the palette
> (both themes), the type scale, the spacing / radius / icon / elevation scales,
> the semantic alias layer, screen composition, responsive rules and the web
> techniques that must not be copied. Everything below assumes it and names
> tokens instead of repeating values.

## Implementation guardrails

Do NOT build a widget. The platform supplies this; configure it. Inspect the repository only to confirm the platform behaviour is
already configured. Reserve whatever inset or barrier the platform reports at
runtime; never turn a dimension below into an app token or a fixed spacer, and
never paint a replacement for it.

THE CALLER OWNS: everything else on the screen.

## Component visual intent — StatusBar

Mock status bar drawn by the preview frame only. Android owns the real one; reserve the inset, never paint this.

## Component contract — StatusBar

Dimensions — label, dimension class, value:
  height              SYSTEM-OWNED    44 · PREVIEW (kit frame chrome, never an app token)
  padding             SYSTEM-OWNED    0 24 · PREVIEW
  content             SYSTEM-OWNED    time + signal/wifi/battery glyphs

FIXED means reproduce the value. MINIMUM means never go below it, grow freely.
MAXIMUM means never exceed it. CONTENT-DRIVEN means the content sets it — do
not convert it into a fixed box, and a content-driven control entering a
loading state keeps the width that instance already had. RESPONSIVE means it
changes with width or text scale. SYSTEM-OWNED means the platform supplies it.
UNSPECIFIED means this design does not determine the value: do not invent one —
keep the repository's existing convention where that is safe, and ask when
geometry, state behaviour, interaction, content loss or accessibility cannot be
settled without an answer.

## Priorities — StatusBar

  P1  the dimension table and the tones/variants above — the component's own
      surface treatment, geometry and type
  P2  its states, icon steps and hairline / shadow treatment
  P3  motion and decorative polish
  Global palette, type scale and spacing rhythm are the FOUNDATIONS run's
  priorities, not this task's.

## Self-check — StatusBar

  mode boundary           PASS
  dimension classes       PASS
  token references        PASS
  ownership               PASS
  web mechanics           PASS
  touch geometry          PASS
  long content            n/a
  loading width           n/a

Everything else (tokens, colour, type, spacing, composition, responsive rules)
comes from the Foundations spec — do not re-derive it from this prompt.

SYSTEM-OWNED — DO NOT IMPLEMENT AS APP UI:

dimensions.value: 0 16 regular · 0 12 small numeric / 0 16 small with a glyph · 0 12 compact · 0 8 chip · 0 36 study action

longContent.rule: ONE line: the button grows horizontally with the label. No wrap, no ellipsis.

longContent.scope: regular, width constrained by the caller (block, or a flex share in a dialog/sheet row)
longContent.rule: the label wraps, centred, to at most two lines and the box grows to fit them. No ellipsis, ever. Tightest slot in the product is a dialog confirm at 360: 126px for the label, 106px with a leading glyph — about 18 Latin or 13 Hangul characters. Past two lines the verb is too long: shorten it (authoring rule, checked with tools/button-fit.html).
ONE line, grows horizontally. Wrapping is out of contract at this height — keep the label to a short verb or a numeric value.
ONE line, grows horizontally. Never constrained in v3 (it sits inline in a banner or an app-bar action row), so it never wraps.
ONE line, always. The chip row scrolls horizontally and the chip never shrinks, so a long label lengthens the chip — it never wraps and never truncates.
ONE line, grows horizontally — it sits centred in a study footer with nothing constraining its width. Same rule as an unconstrained regular button.

responsive.behaviour: labels grow with the OS text scale. Unconstrained instances widen; constrained instances wrap and the box grows (height is MINIMUM). Nothing is clamped and nothing is clipped.
a block button follows the content column; an unconstrained button keeps its intrinsic width

resolvedFromSource: FIXED-height vs wrapping label: the kit CSS sets height + no white-space rule, which in a browser paints a second line outside the box. That is a web artefact, not an intent — and Foundations forbids a fixed box around text. RESOLVED: the height is the painted floor (MINIMUM) and the box grows for a wrapped label. No shipped instance changes, because every shipped label fits one line.

Three sizes vs a shipped fourth: the stylesheet comment says "a 4th size is a smell", but 36 (--memox-size-button-sm) ships in four call sites and Foundations documents it. RESOLVED: 36 is a real Button size (small); it is applied inline in source only because no class modifier was ever added. The stylesheet comment is stale.
Three tones vs a shipped fourth: destructive (--memox-error-fill / --memox-on-error-fill) ships in the tag-delete and trash-delete confirms. RESOLVED: four tones.
COMPONENT OVERRIDE — touch floor: the 36, 32 and 28 sizes are painted below the 48 global minimum on purpose. Scope: painted geometry only; the interactive target stays 48.
